title: Simplicial and grafting compatibility of ordered Cut-chain forests
statement:
Use the simplex category $\Delta$ of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], with $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}$. Write $\langle n\rangle=\{*,1,\ldots,n\}$. For $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, with opposite monotone map $a:[m]\to[n]$, define the ordered pointed map $c_\alpha:\langle n\rangle\to\langle m\rangle$ by sending $j$ to $i$ when $a(i-1)<j\leq a(i)$, and to $*$ otherwise; each non-basepoint fibre has the increasing order. Composition of ordered pointed maps replaces each ordered fibre by the concatenation, in its order, of the preceding fibres, omitting inputs sent to $*$. Thus these maps are operators for the ordinary one-color associative operad, whose operations are ordered finite input lists, including the empty list.

For a finite chain $\sigma=([n_0]\xrightarrow{\alpha_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{\alpha_q}[n_q])$, form its full leveled forest record as follows. At level $k$, put one corolla at each output $i=1,\ldots,n_k$, with ordered input slots the fibre $c_{\alpha_k}^{-1}(i)$, and join slots to the matching output wires at level $k-1$. The initial wires are labeled $1,\ldots,n_0$. Keep corollas with no input slots as nullary vertices. A wire sent to $*$ at the next level terminates there as a discarded wire. Keep these discarded components in the full record. A chosen output tree is obtained by retaining just the ancestors of one selected final output; when $q=0$ it is the selected single wire.

The following compatibility holds for all such chains and all their subchains, including repeated stages and zero ordinals. The external initial wires of the chosen output tree $j$ form, in increasing order, the interval
$$L_j=\{a( j-1)+1,\ldots,a(j)\},\qquad a=a_1\circ\cdots\circ a_q,$$
where $a_k=\alpha_k^{\mathrm{op}}$ and for $q=0$ take $a=\mathrm{id}_{[n_0]}$. This interval may be empty, while its tree retains any nullary vertices. Splitting a chain at a stage reconstructs its chosen output trees by ordered grafting of the earlier output trees into the later ones; branches discarded in the later chain are omitted. The initial-wire lists concatenate in precisely this grafting order.

For every weakly increasing $\theta:[p]\to[q]$, the forest of the restricted chain with stages $[n_{\theta(0)}],\ldots,[n_{\theta(p)}]$ is canonically identified with the following operation on the full record. Restrict to these endpoints, substitute all intervening layers between each pair of consecutive retained stages, and discard intermediate corollas whose outputs are unused in that substitution; mark the corresponding unused retained-stage wires as discarded. A repeated retained stage inserts singleton identity corollas. In particular an inner face contracts the intervening layers by substitution, an outer face removes the endpoint layer, and a degeneracy inserts unary identities. Endpoint removal is performed on the full record before taking ancestors of the new final output; it need not be recoverable from a single previously pruned tree. These identifications preserve the ordered wire labels, commute with successive simplicial restrictions, and commute with splitting and grafting at every retained stage. Consequently every intersection of face, degeneracy and grafting operations agrees after the canonical order-preserving identifications, including the empty-output and empty-input cases. This is a statement about finite ordered forests only; it does not construct a coherent diagram in a target category.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Construction 4.1.2.9 (Cut), printed pp. 462-463, and Definition 4.1.1.3 / Remark 4.1.1.4 (ordered associative operators). proof.text: Fix alpha and its opposite monotone map a. The half-open intervals (a(i-1),a(i)] are pairwise disjoint and occur in increasing order; every j in {1,...,n} lies in at most one of them, and all remaining j go to the basepoint. Therefore the displayed rule defines an ordered pointed map c_alpha, with the induced order on each non-basepoint fibre. The case n=0 or m=0 is included because the relevant intervals are empty. This only unfolds the simplex-category and simplicial-operator definitions.

source.place: Construction 4.1.2.9, ordered Cut formula; finite-ordinal verification written here.

proof.text: For alpha:[n]->[m] and beta:[m]->[ell] in Delta^op, let a:[m]->[n] and b:[ell]->[m] be opposites. The fibre of c_beta over j is the consecutive block b(j-1)+1,...,b(j). Substituting c_alpha into that ordered block replaces each i by the increasing block a(i-1)+1,...,a(i), and concatenates these blocks in increasing i. The result is exactly the interval (a(b(j-1)),a(b(j))], which is the fibre of c_{beta alpha} because (a o b)(j)=a(b(j)). Inputs outside the selected blocks are discarded in both descriptions. Thus c_{beta alpha} is the ordered operadic composite, including empty blocks.

source.place: Construction 4.1.2.9, Cut composition; explicit interval calculation.

proof.text: For a chain, attach at level k one vertex for each output i and attach each input slot to the unique matching wire at level k-1; a slot absent from every fibre is recorded as a discarded wire. Every vertex has exactly one outgoing wire, while every non-discarded incoming slot has exactly one parent. Induction on the number of levels therefore gives a finite leveled forest record, with nullary vertices retained because a zero-length fibre still supplies its corolla. Pruning to the ancestors of one final output is well-defined, and for q=0 it leaves the selected initial wire.

source.place: Construction 4.1.2.9, leveled forest interpretation; finite-record construction written here.

proof.text: Induct on q to compute the external wires of the tree feeding final output j. For q=0 the tree is the single wire j and the interval is {j}. For q>0, the last vertex receives the consecutive intermediate outputs b(j-1)+1,...,b(j), where b=a_q. By the induction hypothesis, the r-th of these outputs has external interval (a_1...a_{q-1}(r-1),a_1...a_{q-1}(r)]. These intervals are consecutive and their ordered union is (a_1...a_q(j-1),a_1...a_q(j)], exactly L_j. If the interval is empty, the vertex and its nullary descendants remain in the pruned tree even though no external wire is present.

source.place: Construction 4.1.2.9, external-input interval; induction on chain length.

proof.text: Split the chain after level r. The earlier record supplies one rooted tree for each intermediate output, and the later record supplies the vertices whose input slots are those outputs. Replacing each such slot by its earlier tree is precisely grafting in increasing slot order. The same interval-union calculation as in the preceding step shows that the resulting external list is the concatenation of the earlier lists in that order. If a later vertex sends an intermediate output to the basepoint, its entire earlier component has no path to the chosen final output and is omitted from the pruned tree, while it remains in the full record.

source.place: Construction 4.1.2.9, ordered grafting and discarded branches.

proof.text: Let theta:[p]->[q] be weakly increasing. Replace each consecutive retained pair theta(s)<=theta(s+1) by the composite of all intervening c-maps. By Step 2 this composite has exactly the ordered fibres obtained by substituting all intervening layers. A corolla whose output is not used by any retained successor is marked discarded; this is exactly the full-record restriction before pruning. If theta(s)=theta(s+1), the composite is an identity map and contributes singleton identity corollas. Hence the restricted forest is canonically the stated operation on the full record, with the same wire labels and nullary vertices.

source.place: Construction 4.1.2.9, restriction to subchains and repeated stages.

proof.text: The preceding construction makes each inner face a substitution of adjacent layers, each outer face a deletion of an endpoint layer followed by pruning, and each degeneracy an inserted identity layer. Applying two restrictions in either order keeps the same retained endpoints and composes the same monotone maps; associativity of ordinary function composition and the interval calculation in Step 2 give the same ordered fibres. Since grafting is itself the same ordered substitution, restriction commutes with splitting and grafting. This also explains why an outer face must be taken on the full record: a branch discarded only at the removed endpoint may feed a surviving output after that endpoint is deleted.

source.place: Construction 4.1.2.9, simplicial faces, degeneracies and grafting compatibility.

proof.text: All constructions are finite and order-preserving, so the canonical identifications are unique: a forest is determined by its vertices, ordered input slots, wire labels and parent incidences, and each of these is preserved by the interval substitutions. Empty output ordinals give no final vertices, empty input fibres give nullary vertices, and repeated stages give identities; the same arguments apply without selecting an element from an empty set. Thus every intersection of face, degeneracy and grafting operations agrees, proving the asserted compatibility for finite ordered forests alone, with no target-category coherence being asserted.

source.place: Construction 4.1.2.9 and boundary-case audit of the finite-forest construction.
